assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity as a chemical principle: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove a target protein catalytically, rather than occupying a site stoichiometrically. This is a genuinely new capability, opens previously undruggable targets, and is explainable to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: The concept and first PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto) are separable from the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism (Handa and Ito) and from later optimisation and structural work (Ciulli, Gray). A three-person prize is possible but requires a choice between the PROTAC concept and the glue mechanism; I would press for what exactly was discovered by whom and when.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials and lenalidomide-class glues are approved, with many independent groups confirming degradation by many ligases. Timing looks right to slightly early for the PROTAC arm.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs, on glue mechanism, or both
Priority and credit between Crews, Deshaies and Sakamoto for the original PROTAC concept
Approved-drug evidence for heterobifunctional degraders is still maturing (from my recollection, not independently verified)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert one base to another with a chemical deaminase fused to a programmable nickase, without double-strand breaks. A clean, principle-based invention with enormous generative potential for therapy and research.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver. Komor and Gaudelli are the lead trainees on the two editor classes, and Nishida and Kondo made an independent related cytidine-deaminase editor. A single-laureate award to Liu is cleanest, though the Nishida-Kondo parallel work raises a credit question.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed across many labs and organisms. Clinical base-editing results are emerging (from memory, not verified). CRISPR itself was recognised in 2020, so the committee must justify that this is a distinct chemical invention.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether this is seen as chemistry or biology
Credit for the parallel Nishida-Kondo editor
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy are still being established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned into solution-processed solar absorbers reaching silicon-class efficiencies within a decade, with remarkable defect tolerance and long carrier diffusion lengths. This is the kind of result I like: a clear physical reason for performance and a technology-opening capability.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park and Snaith drove the solid-state step change, Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also strongly associated. Any three-person selection leaves out serious contributors; credit allocation is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are repeatedly confirmed and commercial scale-up is underway, but operational stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved, which argues for caution on timing.
uncertainties: Long-term device stability and lead content
Which three of Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel
Whether the prize better fits chemistry or physics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electrical detection of single polynucleotides threading a nanopore, culminating in commercial long-read sequencing. A physical measurement principle (ionic current blockade) turned into a chemical analytical tool, close to my own nanodevice interests.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandon, Deamer and Branton demonstrated the first single-strand detection, Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled ratcheting that made sequencing feasible. I am unsure of the current status of some of these researchers, so the exact eligible set needs checking. The ratchet step is a particular conceptual contribution.
assessment.maturity: Long-read nanopore sequencing is widely used and independently validated, so maturity is strong.
uncertainties: Eligibility and current status of some credited individuals is not verified by me
Division of credit among the original detection, pore engineering and motor-enzyme steps
Whether the committee sees it as chemistry or as biotechnology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Scaffolded DNA origami demonstrated that kilobase-scale single-stranded DNA can be folded into arbitrary two-dimensional shapes by staple strands, enabling programmable nanostructures. A conceptually clean principle that opened a large field of molecular engineering.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 paper is the decisive origami contribution. Earlier structural DNA nanotechnology by Seeman is a foundation but is not in the credited set, and Winfree, Yan, Shih and Yin extended the field to algorithmic assembly and 3D structures. A single or two-person citation seems defensible.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and extended, with applications in biophysics and drug delivery; real-world use is still modest compared with the scientific impact.
uncertainties: Relation to Seeman's foundational work, who is not among the credited names
Whether Winfree, Yan, Shih or Yin should share credit
Practical applications are still emerging

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle for membraneless compartments in cells. It links polymer physics with cell biology and changed how we think about intracellular organisation.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's 2009 P-granule work is the founding observation; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction framework, and Pappu and Mittag provided the physical-chemical theory. The decisive trio seems identifiable but contested.
assessment.maturity: The concept is broadly accepted, yet the field is debating how much condensates are functional versus artefacts of overexpression, and its quantitative predictive power is still limited. This is arguably a bit early.
uncertainties: Controversy about physiological relevance of condensates in vivo
Whether the physical-chemical theory or the cell-biological discovery should be recognised
Credit among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics, from shotgun peptide identification to quantitative, deep-coverage protein measurement, transformed chemical analysis of whole proteomes. The broad capability is clear, though the discovery is more a collection of methods than a single principle.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the most common core trio, with Hunt, Gygi and Heck also important. Because the 2002 prize already honoured ionisation methods for biomolecular MS, the committee would have to explain the new step clearly.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and used worldwide, with decades of independent confirmation. The timing is more than adequate, if anything late.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for ESI and MALDI
The field is a set of cumulative method developments, so the single decisive discovery is hard to isolate
Choice of three among six or more credited people

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling provides a general route to aryl amines, central to pharmaceutical synthesis. It is among the most widely used reactions in industrial organic chemistry, although the 2010 cross-coupling prize already covered Pd-catalysed C-C coupling.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general ligand-supported amination; Kosugi's earlier tin amide work is a precursor. Priority between the two main labs is close, which makes the pair a natural but delicate award. Including Kosugi would reflect precedent.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with thousands of independent applications. The main concern is that it may be seen as an extension of the 2010 prize rather than a new discovery.
uncertainties: Perceived as an incremental extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize
Role of Kosugi's precursor work versus the general catalysts
Priority disputes between the Buchwald and Hartwig groups
